newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada to issue new tax-protected savings bonds.
newsitem.headline: Canada to issue new tax-protected savings bonds.

text.p: Finance Minister Paul Martin announced on Thursday the government would be issuing a new tax-protected savings product, the Canada RRSP Bond.

It is designed primarily to catch demand from Canadians during what has become known as "RRSP season," the period up to the end of February when they can put money into registered retirement savings plans (RRSPs) and deduct the amount from their taxes for the previous year's income.
The Canada RRSP Bond will offer guaranteed annual interest rates for 10 years, with annual compound interest on the anniversary of the issue.
The Finance Department said these were the first exclusively retail, investment and savings bonds offered since Canada Savings Bonds in 1946.

They have some similarities to Canada Savings Bonds. Interest rates on the new bonds will rise in each year of their 10-year life -- similar to the Series 51 Canada Savings Bond issued last November 1. But a spokeswoman said the rates will not rise as market conditions warrant, as with the Series 51. To compensate for this, the rates will be higher than otherwise would be the case. Also, the bonds will only be cashable annually, unlike Series 51 which is cashable anytime.
The new bonds will only carry compound interest, not compound or regular interest as with Canada Savings Bonds. Interest can be earned between the date of purchase and the date of issue.
They are only available for registered savings plans.
The new bonds will go on sale from February 3 through April 1, with two issue dates -- March 1 and April 1.

The government is also creating a retirement savings plan, The Canada RSP, to hold Government of Canada non-marketable securities as investments -- both Canada RRSP Bonds and Canada Savings Bonds. The interest rates will be announced later.
